datum: NAVD88 (2004.65 epoch), feet as published; the build converts to metres

ihncLock.what: Hourly staff-gauge stage at the IHNC lock, the only complete record of the canal that morning. IPET publishes it only as a chart; these values were digitized from the chart's vector markers (about +/-0.05 ft; readings above about 12.5 ft were taken to the nearest 0.5 ft).
ihncLock.where: Vol. IV Fig. 14 p. IV-33 and App. 1 Fig. 1-56

at.note: assumed position of the lock, at the river end of the canal

ward.what: Water surface inside the Lower Ninth Ward: the highest level the published interior evidence shows by each time. Before 07:30 the evidence is next to the north breach (Site C1, OP-5); after 07:30 it is Jackson Barracks at the ward's east edge. Arabi, between the parish line and Paris Road, shares this surface: IPET found the Lower Ninth and St. Bernard peaking together at 10.5-11 ft, and Team Louisiana puts Chalmette's high water about 0.5 ft above the Lower Ninth's.
ward.where: Vol. IV pp. IV-194 to IV-199 and Fig. 136 (digitized)
samplesFt: first inflow at Site C1, where the ground is about -6 ft (IPET p. IV-195, IV-198)
Site C1 clocks stop at +2 ft (p. IV-195)
higher Site C1 clocks stop (Fig. 136, digitized)
Jackson Barracks, ground about +4 ft, still dry (p. IV-196); held at the 06:30 level
peak at Jackson Barracks (Fig. 136; text gives 14:45); IPET p. IV-199 gives 10.5-11 ft for the ward

breaches.label: North breach, IHNC east floodwall just south of Florida Ave
breaches.widthNote: IPET V App. 14 p. V-14-23 gives 250 ft; IPET IV App. 9 and the court give 180 ft; ILIT about 250 ft; Team Louisiana 90 ft
breaches.opensNote: IPET's earliest time; ILIT and Team Louisiana say 07:30-07:45, the court about 06:00
breaches.atNote: assumed: about 100 m south of the Florida Ave bridge on the east bank line between the bridges (OpenStreetMap); no source gives coordinates
breaches.speedNote: assumed spreading speed, read from the site positions in IPET Fig. 135 (no coordinates published): water reached Site 4 (Tupelo St), roughly 0.5 km from the breach, by 05:30, and Site C2, roughly 1 km east, only from about 07:30. 8 m a minute reaches Site 4 on time and C2 about an hour early, erring toward earlier deadlines

breaches.label: South breach, IHNC east floodwall from about 300 ft north of N. Claiborne Ave
breaches.widthNote: IPET V App. 14 p. V-14-23 gives 850 ft; IPET IV App. 9 and the court give 793 ft; ILIT nearly 900 ft; Team Louisiana 1,000 ft
breaches.opensNote: Team Louisiana's 'consensus' time; ILIT 07:45; the court about 07:00
breaches.atNote: assumed: centre of an 850 ft stretch starting 300 ft north of the Claiborne Ave bridge on the east bank (OpenStreetMap bridge positions); no source gives coordinates
breaches.speedNote: derived: water reached Jackson Barracks, about 3.1 km away, at about 08:00, 30 minutes after the 07:30 breach (IPET p. IV-196)

wind.what: Only two timed wind observations near the ward survive in the NHC table. Directions are not published.

samples.station: NASA Michoud gage 2, about 40 ft up, unofficial

inflows.label: St. Bernard floodwater from the 40 Arpent overtopping, meeting the ward's water near Paris Road
inflows.opensNote: assumed: IPET p. IV-199 says the IHNC water moving east merged with the Chalmette water 'in the vicinity of Paris Road in the midmorning timeframe'; we take 10:00. Chalmette's water entered from the north-east about 08:20 (IPET p. IV-198), and Team Louisiana dates the 40 Arpent overtopping east of Paris Road from about 08:30 (pp. 80-81)
inflows.speedNote: assumed equal to the south breach's derived speed
